description: A VARCHAR put INTO a container stays a string member, however much its text reads as JSON - and so it comes back out a VARCHAR. This is the write-side twin of the PARSE_JSON rule: PARSE_JSON('"[1,2,3]"') is a string because its argument's TYPE says so, and ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('[1,2]') holds a string for the same reason. Frostlake re-read the text as structure when embedding it, so the element came back an ARRAY and nothing downstream could tell it from a real one; extraction was never at fault, since a container built by PARSE_JSON already returned the right thing. A value that really IS semi-structured is unaffected, and the aggregate builders OBJECT_AGG / ARRAY_AGG follow the same rule - which is where double-encoding used to show up. Converted 1:1 from functions/ContainerStringMemberTest (now retired); its @BeforeEach kv fixture is inlined per test.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE kv (k VARCHAR, v VARCHAR)
